segments.summary: Interview handoff, blocked-state contracts, Assistant worktree scope, Source Control ownership, and accordion persistence were reviewed; gaps center on handoff auditability, blocked-action validation, and persisted-state recovery.

Source Control filter/header/dropdown/binding/storage behavior was reviewed; principal risks are destructive-action confirmation, active-run races, multi-record atomicity, and revalidation error classification.

Frozen file identity, mode invariants, create dialog/backend/results, authority boundary, auto-create, and rename behavior were reviewed; transaction rollback and silent rename failure remain underspecified.
Runtime ownership, settings, icons/projections, and cleanup were reviewed; canonical settings detail, clamp bounds, freshness transitions, and dropdown removal atomicity/safety are unresolved.
Retention, entry routing, merge dialog, guards, recovery, execution context, and locking were reviewed; in-flight Cancel lacks a safe lifecycle contract.

Stale-lock recovery, command strategies, offline fetch, rebase limits, hooks, post-merge behavior, and conflict routing were reviewed; the age-only stale predicate and hook/cancel recovery are critical gaps.

PR, natural-language merge, test settings, command trust, and auto-detection were reviewed; API/panel sequencing, chained cleanup approval, arbitrary-command trust, and missing detection matrix require closure.

First-run gating, strategy test order, dialog execution, abort, environment, crash recovery, and seglog events were reviewed; misleading skipped gates, cancellation, output privacy, recovery, and missing event schemas are material gaps.

cross_document_questions: Which canonical owner embeds the complete Assistant Worktrees settings matrix and numeric bounds promised by ACD-338 and ACD-340?
Which canonical owner defines atomic bind/create/remove transactions and recovery across thread binding, reverse lookup, worktree record, seglog, and projections?
Which canonical owner defines merge/test cancellation, hook-failure cleanup, stale-lock safety, and crash reconciliation as one executable lifecycle?
Which canonical owner defines versioned binding, merge, PR, and test seglog payload schemas with redaction and replay semantics?
